previousCoordinate.reasonReplaced: Legacy-punktet lå omtrent 113 meter sørvest for det navngitte områdepunktet og hadde ingen dokumentert kontrakt til Møllebyen, museet eller et bestemt industribygg.

identity.resolvedIdentity: Møllebyen in Moss, the historic mill and industrial district at Mossefossen, with Moss by- og industrimuseum as a visitor and interpretation component inside the district.
identity.identityProblem: The place name combines a district and a museum. The coordinate must represent the historic industrial area without collapsing it into the museum entrance, the waterfall, one mill building, the library or the nearby Moss Ironworks and Convention House.
identity.splitReason: The district and museum belong in one composite place because the museum interprets the same industrial environment. They remain separate anchors and access objects inside the record.

requiredEvidence: named district entity or independent district coordinate
museum identity and address as a separate component
dating of the surviving industrial buildings
industrial decline and adaptive reuse chronology
separation from Moss Ironworks and the Convention House

evidence.finding: Q28719372 identifies Møllebyen in Moss at 59.43900, 10.66800 and describes the former industrial area at Mossefossen that is now used for museum, library, cinema, galleries, restaurants and businesses.
evidence.reason: Provides an independent named-area entity and coordinate within a few dozen metres of the applied district point.

evidence.finding: Identifies Møllebyen as the area by Mossefossen, mainly along Henrik Gerners gate, and gives the coordinate 59.43843, 10.66789. It describes nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century mill and factory buildings, the Lilleelv watercourse, decline, rehabilitation after 1998 and new cultural and commercial uses.
evidence.reason: Direct independent coordinate for the district and a clear entity description matching the place.

evidence.finding: Places the museum in an old mill building in Møllebyen beside Mossefossen at Fossen 21/23 and presents waterpower, labour, machines and people as central to more than 300 years of Moss history.
evidence.reason: Confirms the museum as an active component and visitor anchor, not the full district coordinate.

evidence.sourceName: Wikidata and Wikimedia Commons – Moss by- og industrimuseum
evidence.finding: Identifies the museum at approximately 59.43861, 10.66806, inside the Møllebyen district and close to the applied district coordinate.
evidence.reason: Useful as a component control while the wider district remains canonical.

evidence.finding: Confirms the registered museum unit and the address Fossen 21-23, Møllebyen, 1530 Moss.
evidence.reason: Authoritative current address control for the museum component.

evidence.finding: Describes Møllebyen by Mossefossen as a successful example of new use of old industrial buildings, now containing library, cinema, museum, restaurants, homes and offices.
evidence.reason: Supports the district identity and current mixed-use limitations.

evidence.finding: Describes likely mill activity from the medieval period, surviving brick industrial buildings mainly from 1875-1920, Moss as the third-largest mill town in Norway in the late nineteenth century, industrial relocation, the 1971 fire, rehabilitation after 1998 and completion of major adaptive reuse by 2003.
evidence.reason: Supports the historical layers and prevents year 1700 from being misread as the construction year of the standing buildings.

evidence.finding: The legacy point lies approximately 113.0 metres south-west of the applied district coordinate and does not identify a named area or component.
evidence.reason: Rejected because it lacks an entity and source-object contract.

sourceObjectCandidates.rejectionReason: Matching district entity and control coordinate; the applied Lokalhistoriewiki point is slightly more precise and directly stated for the district.
The museum is a component and visitor anchor, not the whole Møllebyen district.
The waterfall is the power source and landscape context, not the historic industrial district itself.
Moss Ironworks and the Convention House are a nearby but separate canonical place.

rawEvidence.description: Persisted district and museum coordinates, area identity, address controls, industrial chronology, adaptive reuse and access limitations.

decision.nextAction: Applied the named Møllebyen district coordinate, retained the museum as a separate visitor anchor and continue with folkenborg_museum.

notes: The coordinate moves approximately 113 metres north-east.
The historic industrial district is canonical; the museum is a component.
Year 1700 is a rounded historical layer, not the construction year of the standing buildings.
Mossefossen and Lilleelv are power and watercourse components.
The radius is not a district, property, building, museum, business, water, safety, heritage or access boundary.
